To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and validated an in-cell screening assay to identify small molecules (EPMs), which reduce bacterial load and synergize with host innate immunity to kill MDR Gram-negative bacterial pathogens.
an in-cell screening platform was used to discover three efflux pump inhibitors that synergize with antibiotics to kill bacteria.
an in-cell screening assay identified three efflux modulators that synergize with antimicrobial peptides and antibiotics to inhibit bacterial growth and survival in host cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel antibacterials with activity against MDR Gram-negative pathogens.
the development of new antimicrobial agents to address the global problem of antibiotic resistance.
the identification of small molecules that inhibit efflux pump activity and increase the efficacy of antimicrobial peptides and antibiotics against Gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three putative EPIs demonstrated significant antibacteri- al activity against Salmonella and inhibited efflux pumps in Salmonella and MDR Gram-negative pathogens.

the in-cell screening platform described in this study can be used to discover new classes of antibacterial compounds that can kill bacteria and that have the potential for development into new antibiotics.
this study demonstrates that a cell based screening platform can identify efflux pump modulator that can be used to kill pathogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EPMs are novel antibacterial compounds that inhibit efflux pump activity, synergize with antibiotics and innate immunity, and have potential for the development of novel anti-infective agents.
an in-cell screening platform was used to identify small molecules with antibacterial activity against Gram-negative bacteria.

an in-cell screening platform identified EPMs with antibacterial activity in macrophages, synergy with antimicrobial peptide, and inhibition of AcrAB-Tolerance to multiple antibiotics in broth and in infected macrophages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an in-cell screening platform identified EPMs with potential as adjuvans to antibiotics and as synergizers with antimicrobial peptides.
an in-cell assay can identify efflux pump modulator (EPM) compounds that reduce bacterial load within infected host cells.

the screening platform is a useful tool for identifying small molecules that inhibit bacterial replication and survival within host cells and that the EPMs identified in the screen have potential for development to treat bacterial infections.
